title: The head injury, cancer and the nickname Half-a-Head
summary: A baseball hit at age eleven led to a cancer diagnosis and nine months of experimental treatment, and the nickname Half.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Just going back through my list here, how did you get the nickname Half Ahead?

Well, that's something I was just mentioning about when I was 11 years old and I was playing baseball on the altar boys team. I was an altar boy for Corpus Christi. One day we were playing ball and a baseball hit me in the side of my head causing a tumor, a sebaceous cyst. And it was extracted, analyzed, and found out to be cancer. I was 11 years old. This was 51 years ago. No, 52 years, 53 years now. I'm back. Anyhow, at this time I was put in the hospital and like I said, he extracted the tumor and he took it to a lab and he analyzed it and so forth. And then the doctor came back and he explained to my mother that this tumor was a very new and detrimental disease at the time because people knew nothing about and they didn't know very much about cancer then in those days and how to arrest it and so forth and so on. So this doctor was doing his internship at Charity Hospital and he got my mother to give him permission to do an experimental operation on me. And that was to take this tumor from my head and extract all things around it for a certain area and then give me treatment with this ultraviolet light that was just being invented. That ultraviolet light today is chemotherapy. That doctor's name today is Dr. Michael DeBakey. Good God.
Yeah. He was here in New Orleans? Yes.
I think he was here. He studied at Charity Hospital and he is responsible for that.
That's amazing. And it was a very successful operation. Obviously. I happened to be one of the oldest cancer survivors. Hmm.
Well if you hadn't had that accident been hit in the head then they wouldn't have discovered the cancer? Probably? Until it was...
If I would have had the accident it wouldn't have happened at all.
Oh so the accident caused the cancer?

The ball. The ball. The ball hitting me in the head caused this... It was something. Yeah. Okay. It caused the tumor. Okay. You see the tumor became infected and took on whatever basis at that time to become cancer because it was in the early stages of people having things happen to them and this cancer was at a very early stage. I mean we talking about the year of 19... 42, 43.

43. You know. We talking about 1943. Right. Nobody knew about cancer in 43. Yeah. I mean like I say the chemotherapy that was given to me then it was the big ultra-violent light and they put you in this room and they would wrap you up in a blanket of lead. Even the people who came in to put the things on, put the turn it on and so forth. And they put my head in this leather and leaded shielded contraption so that only a little part of my head the light would shine on. And I used to have that treatment done to me say for instance three times a week while I was in the hospital. I was in the hospital for nine months in Charity Hospital. And I wasn't on the children's ward because no children were being affected with anything like that. So I was on the surgery ward with the older men. Yeah. Me and a little boy running around with all the older guys that was in the hospital. And I got to be there.
How did that all affect you when you got out as a young kid over the years?

Huh? I can't really recall how it affected me because by being only eleven and twelve years old, stuff like stuff stuff like stuff stuff like stuff stuff like the top of it and so forth. For a long time, even to a young man of 20 some odd years old, the inferior complex followed me by being in public and people staring at me and so forth. And there was a schoolmate. He said he succumbed to cancer not three years ago. His name was Edward Rodney, one of my best friends, and he used to call me Half.
Yeah, just Half. Just Half. Yeah. And some of them called me Half-A-Head and so forth. But if anybody comes along right now and says that to me, I know it's got to be one of my childhood friends.
